task_info.original_instruction:
Search for the paper "AgentPoison: Red-teaming LLM Agents via Poisoning Memory or Knowledge Bases" using Semantic Scholar API.

Extract the **GitHub repository URL** from the paper's abstract or metadata.

**IMPORTANT Requirements:**
1. The URL must be a GitHub repository link in the format: https://github.com/username/repository
2. The URL must be a valid Git repository that can be cloned using `git clone`
3. DO NOT use project homepage URLs (like https://....github.io/ or documentation sites)
4. DO NOT use artifact/release URLs
5. Look for phrases like "code is available at", "our implementation", "github.com/", etc.

**Example of correct URLs:**
- ✓ https://github.com/username/project-name
- ✓ https://github.com/organization/repo-name
- ✗ https://username.github.io/project (project homepage, NOT a repository)
- ✗ https://huggingface.co/... (not GitHub)

Save the GitHub repository URL to /app/git_url.txt (one URL per line).

Use the available tools to search for the paper and extract the correct GitHub repository URL.

In this paper, we introduce AgentPoison, a novel framework for red-teaming LLM agents by poisoning their memory or knowledge bases. We demonstrate that by inserting malicious data into an agent's memory or knowledge store, adversaries can manipulate the agent's behavior without directly interacting with the LLM's prompt interface. Our approach exploits the reliance of modern LLM agents on external knowledge sources and memory mechanisms. We propose two poisoning attack methods: (1) memory poisoning, which corrupts the agent's episodic memory to cause misbehavior in future interactions, and (2) knowledge base poisoning, which injects false information into retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems. Through extensive experiments on various agent benchmarks, we show that AgentPoison can significantly degrade agent performance and induce harmful outputs. tool_params.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents are increasingly being deployed in real-world applications, raising significant security concerns. In this paper, we introduce AgentPoison, a novel framework for red-teaming LLM agents by poisoning their memory or knowledge bases. We demonstrate that by inserting malicious data into an agent's memory or knowledge store, adversaries can manipulate the agent's behavior without directly interacting with the LLM's prompt interface. Our approach exploits the reliance of modern LLM agents on external knowledge sources and memory mechanisms. We propose two poisoning attack methods: (1) memory poisoning, which corrupts the agent's episodic memory to cause misbehavior in future interactions, and (2) knowledge base poisoning, which injects false information into retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems. Through extensive experiments on various agent benchmarks, we show that AgentPoison can significantly degrade agent performance and induce harmful outputs. Our code is available at https://github.com/janhu95/AgentPoison and our dataset will be released publicly to facilitate further research on LLM agent security.
tool_params.title: AgentPoison: Red-teaming LLM Agents via Poisoning Memory or Knowledge Bases
